frustrations.description: Things they're fed up with or tired of dealing with.
examples: Sick of busting my butt and still feeling broke.

wants.description: What they really want in life — stuff that keeps them going.
examples: I just want to have enough so I don't stress every month.

dreams.description: Big picture, what they hope their life looks like in the future.
examples: Owning a few properties and chilling on a beach somewhere.

fears.description: What freaks them out or keeps them up at night.
examples: What if I lose everything? Like, what if the market crashes tomorrow?

suspicions.description: What they're skeptical or unsure about.
examples: Is my real estate agent really looking out for me, or just making a sale?

insecurities.description: Their inner doubts, stuff they might not admit.
examples: What if I'm just not cut out for this investing stuff?

envy_feelings.description: What makes them jealous of others.
examples: Man, seeing people my age already retired and living it up kinda stings.

enemies.description: The people, things, or situations holding them back.
examples: The constant rise in property prices makes it feel like I'll never catch up.

coping_mechanism.description: How they cope with their frustrations, fears, and insecurities — what they do to avoid the pain.
examples: I just binge-watch Netflix to escape the stress, or hit the bars with friends to forget about money worries.

hidden_beliefs.description: What they think is true but might be surprised to learn otherwise — commonly held assumptions that could be challenged.
examples: You need a ton of money to start investing in real estate
Only rich people can make it in this game.

emotional_triggers.description: The most emotionally charged words, phrases, or concepts that instantly grab their attention and create strong reactions.
examples: Financial freedom
passive income
being broke
missing out
too late to start

success_markers.description: What they consider proof that they're 'making it' — the visible signs of progress or achievement they desperately want to show others.
examples: Having my first rental property
Getting that first $1K passive income month
Quitting my day job

regulatory_focus_orientation.description: Whether the audience is promotion-focused (seeking gains, growth, ideals) or prevention-focused (avoiding losses, fulfilling duties, seeking safety).
examples: PROMOTION: 'I want to build something incredible'
PREVENTION: 'I need to protect what I have'

moral_foundation_violated.description: Which of Haidt's 6 Moral Foundations is activated — reverse-engineered from moral emotion linguistic signatures.
examples: FAIRNESS: 'This system is rigged'
CARE: 'These kids deserve better'

coping_trajectory_position.description: Current phase in the Lazarus & Folkman stress-coping cycle. SEARCH_PHASE = peak intervention receptivity.
examples: SEARCH: 'Has anyone tried this?'
ACTIVE: 'I've been working on it step by step'

hermeneutical_gap_markers.description: Evidence of unarticulated experience — discourse truncation, affective parabola, metaphor novelty.
examples: TRUNCATION: 'It's like... I don't know...'
NOVELTY: 'It felt like being underwater but I could still breathe'

reconsolidation_sensitivity.description: Readiness for memory reconsolidation — prediction error sensitivity and engagement depth.
examples: HIGH PE: 'I never thought of it that way'
SAVE: 'Bookmarking this'

dreams: Owning the Most Luxurious Home in the Neighborhood
Becoming the Leading Real Estate Investor
insecurities: Not being cut out for this
hidden_beliefs: You need a ton of money to start
